summary: Tested the Telegram second chat ID feature (telegram_chat_id_2). Backend: 22/22 pytest passed. That covers 11 unit tests of notify fan-out with _send_one/_send_document_one mocked (configure/dedupe/explicit chat/partial failure with warning/send_detailed per-chat results/all-fail raises/no chats raises/send_document fan-out/notify kind toggle) and 11 API tests (persisting both IDs with chats_count=2, global config visible on /api/fx and /api/pepper, clearing the 2nd ID gives count 1, 41 chars gives 422 on /api and /api/fx, PUT via /api/fx/config also works, /telegram/test without a token gives 424 'Telegram no configurado' on /api, /api/fx and /api/pepper, /telegram/chats without a token gives 400). UI on /bybit Settings: both fields and hint render; the same ID in both fields shows telegram-same-chat-error, and Guardar shows an error toast and does not save (config unchanged); different IDs → 'Telegram guardado' toast and config 555/666 count 2; the Quitar button shows only when field 2 has text and empties it; both Detectar buttons → 'Introduce el token del bot primero' toast, no crash; Enviar prueba is disabled and there is no ready badge (no token). /hotforex and /pepperstone Settings show the same saved values. Config restored to empty with enabled=false.
critical_code_review_comments: The 'Conectado · 2 chats' badge could not be checked in the UI: it needs a real token (telegram_ready). The code logic looks correct.
Only console errors were the 2 expected 400 responses from the Detectar chat ID calls made without a token.
The same-ID check is client-side only: the backend silently dedupes when chat_id_2 equals chat_id (harmless, since dedupe means a single delivery).
seed_data_creation: None. Telegram config set temporarily to 111/222, 555/666 and 333, then restored to empty with enabled=false.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Telegram config is global (gstore); /api/fx/config and /api/pepper/config merge it in. No real Telegram token is available. Bots were not started and AI settings were not touched.
